verdicts.rationale: Constructor defines the function type stored by Registry.Register, whose code enforces the admission rules for that type. These are the contract and registration path for service constructors.
RegisterAll explicitly binds the heartbeat service name to NewHeartbeatService in its Constructor map. The catalogue entry and implementation jointly expose that built-in service.

The package documentation names the startup-unit gauge and its stage counts, while newStartupMetricWriter constructs that exact metric with owner/stage labels. The separate file documents the writer's metric responsibility.
resolveServiceConfigs materializes metrics configuration with the path and port consumed and defaulted by NewMetrics. Their matching keys and values show a shared default metrics-service setup.

HTTPHandler declares the mounting contract implemented by StorageObservabilityService.RegisterHTTPHandlers, and the compile-time assertion confirms the implementation. This interface and method belong together when changing the report's HTTP surface.

Configurable declares ConfigSchema and explicitly names Metrics as an implementer; Metrics.ConfigSchema states that it implements that discovery interface. They carry one service-configuration discovery contract.

OpenAPISpec carries reflected request/response types for schema generation, and SchemaFromType generates JSON Schema from reflected types. The declaration and generator are complementary pieces of the OpenAPI schema responsibility.

ManagerConfig's ServerInfo field is typed InfoSpec, which defines the API metadata also used by OpenAPIDocument. Configuration changes to those metadata fields require the type definition alongside the containing configuration.
Health directly asserts deliveryFatalReporter on the subscriber, and the interface comment explains this health-read seam. These symbols implement the same delivery-failure health observation.
preflightRulePackMutations invokes the ProjectionBinder preflight and binding methods and validates their contracts. This implements the interface's stated validation-before-injection responsibility.

The shared small-config shape and boilerplate comment mask separate listeners: the metrics service's port/path versus the Manager HTTP server's API and Swagger settings. Combining them would misidentify the configuration surface.

Both methods share the Validate name and configuration-validity boilerplate. Heartbeat validation governs its interval, whereas log-forwarder validation delegates min-level/source-filter policy for a separate service.

Both register named values in mutex-protected maps, but one catalogues constructors for service composition and the other catalogues OpenAPI specifications. Their registry shape serves different responsibilities.

Both assemble properties and required fields under schema terminology. NewConfigSchema builds service configuration-discovery metadata, while schemaFromStruct reflects a type into a JSON Schema object.
The cited Stop methods share lifecycle synchronization and terminal-state scaffolding. Their remaining source cleans up different service resources: a metrics server versus a milestone subscriber.

Both start diagnostic HTTP listeners, but the pprof source explicitly rejects lifecycle-managed Service ownership. Metrics.Start participates in service lifecycle and failure rollback, so matching start-server vocabulary would conceal that distinction.

Both handlers use GET-only JSON response scaffolding. serveGraphTriples returns queried graph triples, whereas handleReport serializes an existing storage-report snapshot; the endpoint responsibilities differ.
The immediate emission and ticker/select loops have the same periodic shape. One emits heartbeat logs while the other re-evaluates stream migration-override expiry, so the subjects are separate.
The register name is overloaded: one registers a Prometheus gauge and the other mounts an HTTP report route. The cited calls target different registration systems and responsibilities.

Both classify changes into operation strings, but detectKVOperation labels an individual KV event and pendingServiceChanges compares boot and desired service configuration. Event observation and composition drift are distinct subjects.
